chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:
Three [acts] from the practices of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance): pride in lineage, vilification due to status, and seeking rain through the anwaa' (star positions).
ai.seo_question: What are the three acts of the Jahiliyyah mentioned by Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies three characteristic practices of the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah that persisted or were considered part of it: pride in one's lineage, criticizing others' lineages, and seeking rain by observing the positions of stars (anwaa'). This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, highlights how these specific social and astrological behaviors were viewed as remnants of ignorance that Islam sought to eradicate, linking them to the broader concept of *Jahiliyyah* as a state of spiritual and social misguidance rather than merely a historical period.
